stances.claim: The PPCRV and its half-million volunteers deserve the nation's gratitude on the same plane as Comelec, DepEd, and the PNP for assuring orderly and peaceful elections -- and uniquely so because, unlike paid Election Board chairs (P6,000), members (P5,000), Deso (P4,000), and staff (P2,000), the PPCRV volunteers served unpaid out of 'selfless desire to safeguard our democracy.'

PPCRV's nonpartisan credibility -- demonstrated by validating the 1992 election of Protestant Ramos despite Catholic opposition -- is the precise reason close-margin victories (Ramos won with only 23.58% and a plurality of 874,348) have been peacefully accepted in PH; the PPCRV is, in effect, infrastructure for elite consensus on electoral outcomes.

Myla C. Villanueva, despite taking PPCRV's presidency late in the 2019 election season, was a 'perfect fit' -- prodigious and computer-savvy, fluent in the automated election system -- and the 'reward for good work is more work' as the digital election age accelerates.

Justice Henri Jean Paul B. Inting deserves welcome despite his junior CA standing because he rose from the lowest rungs (Metropolitan TC, Regional TC, CA, SC), accumulated longer total bench years than many former colleagues, and left his appellate docket with no backlog -- qualities likely to help trim SC case congestion.
His co-nominees need not despair: four more 2019 vacancies are coming (Del Castillo, Jardeleza, Carpio, Bersamin), and possibly a fifth if Bersamin is replaced by an insider.

notable_anecdotes: CJ's parenthetical disclosure: 'From among the PCP II lay delegates, I was chosen PPCRV's national vice chair and chief legal counsel until 1995, when I joined the Supreme Court' -- a self-implication that converts the column from outside praise into inside testimony.

The PCP II logistics -- 145 lay leaders in daily 12-hour sessions from January 20 to February 17, 1991, at the San Carlos Lay Formation Center in Makati -- physicalizing the institutional labor that produced PPCRV.

The Ramos-1992 reception arithmetic -- Ramos a Protestant 'opposed by some Catholic organizations, priests and bishops' won with only 23.58% and a plurality of 874,348 over his closest rival -- yet 'our people accepted his victory because, according to Ramos himself, it was validated by an independent and credible PPCRV.' The detail that Ramos himself credited PPCRV makes the credibility claim self-authenticating.

Justice Inting's career inversion: 'still a junior member of the Court of Appeals when elevated' yet with 'much longer years in the bench than many of his former colleagues' -- the lowest-rung-to-highest-court career arc as institutional argument.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban thanks the Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting (PPCRV) and its half-million volunteers for helping ensure orderly 2019 polls -- a contribution he places on the same plane as Comelec, the Department of Education, and the Philippine National Police. Unlike the paid Election Board chairs (P6,000), members (P5,000), DepEd supervising officers (P4,000), and staff (P2,000), PPCRV volunteers served without compensation, sustained only by 'selfless desire to safeguard our democracy.' He traces PPCRV's origin to 1991, when the Second Plenary Council of the Philippines -- meeting daily for 12-hour sessions from January 20 to February 17 at the San Carlos Lay Formation Center in Makati -- for the first time in the Church's 2,000-year history invited 145 lay leaders to legislate alongside the hierarchy in implementing Vatican II in the Philippines. Led by former PH ambassador to the Vatican Henrietta 'Tita' T. De Villa and encouraged by Jaime Cardinal Sin, the laity organized PPCRV; CJ himself served as PPCRV national vice chair and chief legal counsel until joining the SC in 1995. He demonstrates PPCRV's credibility through the 1992 Ramos election: a Protestant who won with only 23.58% and a plurality of 874,348 over his closest rival, opposed by some Catholic organizations and bishops, nonetheless saw his victory accepted because, in Ramos's own words, it was validated by an 'independent and credible PPCRV.' He traces the succession from De Villa (retired 2016) through former Comelec commissioner Rene Sarmiento (resigned August 2018 for health) to current president Myla C. Villanueva -- 'prodigious and computer-savvy' -- and notes that 'the reward for good work is more work' as the digital age advances. He then welcomes Justice Henri Jean Paul B. Inting, newly elevated to the SC despite junior CA standing because he rose from the lowest rungs (Metropolitan TC, RTC, CA, SC) with longer total bench years than many former colleagues and left his appellate docket with no backlog. He closes by consoling Inting's co-nominees with four more 2019 vacancies -- Justices Del Castillo (July 29), Bersamin (Oct. 18), Jardeleza (Sept. 26), and Carpio (Oct. 26) -- and a possible fifth if Bersamin is replaced by an insider.
